findings.text: Legacy mapping entry copies a six word user block into kernel space and rejects file offsets that are not page aligned, then forwards address length protection flags descriptor and page numbered offset to the shared page offset mapping implementation. The direct page offset entry forwards its arguments unchanged to the same common implementation.
Legacy argument block is a sequence of six address sized slots holding target address followed by length protection flags descriptor and byte offset in that order.

Mapping permission derivation starts from protection bits combined with file and flag bits. Anonymous maps gain read may write may and execute may capabilities. Private file maps either inherit masked direct capabilities when direct mapping is allowed or gain the same three may capabilities, plus overlay may when write protection is absent and no tracer is attached. Shared file maps are marked shared and may share and inherit masked direct capabilities. Involved identifiers are PROT_WRITE with MAP_PRIVATE with NOMMU_MAP_DIRECT with NOMMU_VMFLAGS with VM_SHARED with VM_MAYSHARE with VM_MAYREAD with VM_MAYWRITE with VM_MAYEXEC with VM_MAYOVERLAY.

Shared file mapping without memory management attempts direct device mapping first and on success considers the region fully mapped. A not implemented signal from direct mapping is converted to a device error for shared maps because a private copy is not allowed, while other errors propagate. Private maps also attempt direct mapping when allowed and verify shared state, falling back to a private copy only on the not implemented signal and propagating other errors. Involved status names are ENOSYS with ENODEV.

Private copy construction sizes the reservation from the requested length rounded up to power of two order, optionally trims the reservation when excess pages reach a threshold, allocates exact pages, accounts the total, marks mapped copy, initializes region and area start end and top bounds, then either loads file content from the area page offset and zeroes any short tail or marks the area anonymous when no file is present. Involved identifiers are VM_MAPPED_COPY with PAGE_SHIFT.

Private copy allocation failure reports the failing length with process identity, dumps memory state and returns out of memory without creating a mapping. File read failure releases the reserved page series and clears region and area bounds to zero before propagating the read error.

Default guard separation between a growing stack and its neighbor is two hundred fifty six pages. A boot command line option accepts a decimal page count and scales it by page size to override the default, ignoring values with trailing characters.

Upward and downward stack expansion require the address space write lock on entry and assert it, then take the target area write lock and the anonymous reverse map write lock while mutating bounds and the mapping tree, releasing anonymous lock and iterator resources before validation and return.

Upward growth requires grows up marking and a page aligned address below the task size limit with guard separation to the next accessible neighbor. Page offset wrap and accounting failure leave the area unchanged. On success the area end advances and locked and statistical accounting reflect the added pages. Involved bounds are TASK_SIZE with PAGE_MASK with PAGE_SIZE with stack_guard_gap.

Downward growth requires grows down marking and a page aligned address at or above both the minimum mmap address and the first user address, with guard separation from a preceding accessible non growing area. Growth beyond the starting page offset and accounting failure leave the area unchanged. On success the area start retreats and the page offset is reduced by the grown page count with accounting updated. Involved bounds are mmap_min_addr with FIRST_USER_ADDRESS with PAGE_MASK with stack_guard_gap.

Stack growth accounting denies expansion that exceeds expandable space, the stack resource limit, future lock limits, or that would enter a hugetlb only range, with the new start computed from the end minus size except for grows up areas where the existing start is used. Overcommit permission is checked last because it updates security statistics. Involved limit name is RLIMIT_STACK.

Locked stack lookup aligns the address to page boundary and returns the containing area when present. Otherwise one configuration expands the predecessor area while the other expands the successor area starting at or after the address, returning null on expansion failure and populating the newly covered range when the expanded area is locked. Upward versus downward expansion selection is configuration dependent.

User unmap entry strips address tags and requests unmapping with userfault completion handling. Kernel unmap entry requests the same range without that completion mode. Both converge on a common unmap implementation that takes the address space write lock in killable mode and reports interruption on signal.

Unmapping and brk style creation hold the address space write lock across mutation and complete userfault notifications after unlock, with interruption reported when the killable acquisition fails. Deprecated file page remapping first inspects under read lock, releases before security checks, then reacquires write lock and revalidates area flags and file identity before mutation.

Deprecated file page remapping only operates on shared areas, rejects nonzero protection input and unaligned or wrapping ranges, derives effective protection from existing read write and execute markings, forces shared fixed and populate modes while preserving nonblock and locked hints, requires contiguous same file and same flag coverage across any spanned areas, delegates to the common map path, populates on request, and normalizes numeric success to zero. Involved identifiers are MAP_NONBLOCK with MAP_SHARED with MAP_FIXED with MAP_POPULATE with MAP_LOCKED with PROT_READ with PROT_WRITE with PROT_EXEC.

Brk style flags creation aligns the request up, rejects wrap around, treats zero length as success without action, checks brk limits, clears the target range, creates the new area after the predecessor with execute marking derived from the caller flag, and populates when the address space default requires locking.

Address space teardown proceeds from notifier release and read phase cache flush and full gathering with unmapping, to write phase page table release and full area teardown with out of memory killer skipping enabled. An empty area set takes a short path that skips gathering and unmapping and goes directly to structure destruction and unaccounting.
Range teardown accounts pages of areas marked accountable, marks each area detached and removes it while yielding the processor, and warns when the removed count differs from the recorded map count.

Special mapping behavior is defined by a table binding close fault remap and name operations with remote access disabled and split vetoed. Close name and remap delegate to private hooks when present, with remap validating current address space ownership. Identity holds when both the private pointer and the operation table match. Fault handling delegates to a private hook when present, otherwise selects a page by skipping the fault offset through the private page list, takes a reference on success and reports bus error when exhausted. Splitting is always rejected to preserve expected page count alongside no expand marking.

Special mapping installation provides an inserted area carrying caller flags merged with address space defaults plus no expand marking and soft dirty when supported, with locked hints cleared and page protection derived from final flags. The range starts at the requested address with page numbered offset and the private data and operation table attached. Allocation or insertion failure yields an error pointer without insertion, while success accounts pages and emits a mapping event.

Full unmapping initializes a descriptor spanning the whole user range with page table bounds from first user address to user ceiling and tree reset at the first area end in unlocked mode. Page table release initialization repositions the iterator at the saved reset point and narrows area bounds to the page table ceiling range. Involved bounds are FIRST_USER_ADDRESS with USER_PGTABLES_CEILING with ULONG_MAX.
Iterator range limiting for predecessor and successor searches delegates to the underlying maple range primitives with a minimum or maximum bound respectively.
Unmapped area lookup without extra area flags delegates to the flag aware variant with an empty flag set.
Full address space gather helper requests gathering in full mode for the given address space.
